subject: Hosted API upsell: monthly commit step-up & soft-throttle playbook
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmetech.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:10:00 +0000
Subject: Hosted API upsell: monthly commit step-up & soft-throttle playbook

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As discussed, Acme's monthly ingestion spike has consistently exceeded the current hosted commit band for the last two months, and we sketched a conservative upgrade path to avoid soft throttling during Black Week.

Attached is a concise playbook with: a proposed monthly commit step-up (from 1.2M tokens to 1.8M), a temporary burst window for seasonality, and a soft-throttle policy that preserves tail latency for critical routes. Key points: 
- New monthly commit: 1.8M tokens/month (12-month term)
- Burst pocket: +30% for two months during peak (no extra charge for first use)
- Rate bands adjusted to remove hard caps below p95 latency target

Pricing is in the attachment (redwood_pricing_stepup_q3_v2.pdf). We can do a mid-term start date (Aug 1) or align with your next billing cycle on Jul 15 — whichever minimizes proration for Acme.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm preferred start date (Jul 15 or Aug 1)
2) Approve the attached pricing and the soft-throttle policy in principle
3) If approved, I’ll loop in Jordan (rev ops) to push a short addendum and Aisha to coordinate onboarding changes and quota updates

If useful, I can give you a 20-minute run-through of the playbook tomorrow.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_pricing_stepup_q3_v2.pdf

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmetech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@acmetech.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API upsell: monthly commit step-up & soft-throttle playbook

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the summary and the clear options. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop in procurement: 

1) Usage overages: If we go over the 30% burst pocket, how will overages be handled? Is there a per-token overage rate or automatic temporary upgrade?
2) SLA implications: Does the soft-throttle policy change our SLA guarantees for latency on the core /generate route? We need assurance that p99 latency for logged-in users won’t regress during peak.
3) Credits: You mentioned a one-time carryover credit for first burst — can you confirm the credit size and whether that is applied as billing credit or invoice adjustment?

Contracts asked for a redline-ready addendum and a marked-up MSA to attach to our PO. Can you send the redline?

We’re leaning toward Jul 15 start to align with our July billing run, but procurement will confirm once we have answers above.

Thanks —
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Technologies

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmetech.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API upsell: monthly commit step-up & soft-throttle playbook

On Tue, 29 Jun 2027 at 09:42, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmetech.com> wrote:
> 1) Usage overages: If we go over the 30% burst pocket, how will overages be handled? Is there a per-token overage rate or automatic temporary upgrade?
> 2) SLA implications: Does the soft-throttle policy change our SLA guarantees for latency on the core /generate route?
> 3) Credits: You mentioned a one-time carryover credit for first burst — can you confirm the credit size and whether that is applied as billing credit or invoice adjustment?

Great questions — answers below. I’ve attached the redline-ready addendum Jordan prepared for quick signature (MSA_redline_acme_20270630.docx).

1) Overages: We bill overages at the contracted overage rate (0.0008 USD/token for the remaining tokens beyond the burst). We can also include an automatic emergency buffer that temporarily moves you to the next rate band for up to 48 hours if you hit >150% of the new commit; that must be enabled in the addendum and is billable at a blended rate.

2) SLA: The soft-throttle policy is designed not to affect the committed p95/p99 latency guarantees for your Tier. In practice, we deprioritize large low-priority background requests and preserve priority for interactive logged-in routes so p99 for your core route should hold. We will add a clause in the addendum that guarantees the p99 latency SLO for the /generate route except in force majeure or customer-directed degradation.

3) Credit: The one-time burst credit = $10,000 applied as an invoice credit on the first post-start invoice. I’ve flagged this in the addendum for explicit line-item treatment so procurement sees it.

Jordan — can you confirm the minimal contract actions required to effect the step-up if Acme confirms Jul 15? Also Aisha — once signed we’ll need a short ops window to increase quotas and update throttles on the routes.

Thanks —
Kim

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmetech.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 16:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API upsell: monthly commit step-up & soft-throttle playbook

Hi Liam / Kim —

Quick note from RevOps: to implement a Jul 15 start we need a signed addendum (attached) by close of business Jul 8 to avoid any proration gap. The actual operational steps are minimal and we can do the quota change overnight on the requested start date (approx 1–2 hours maintenance window, no downtime).

I confirm the following will be in the addendum:
- Start date: Jul 15, 2027 (customer-selectable)
- New monthly commit: 1.8M tokens/month
- Burst pocket: +30% for two months (one-time $10k invoice credit applied to first invoice)
- Overage rate: $0.0008/token beyond burst; emergency auto-upgrade available (48h max)
- SLA clause: explicit p99 { /generate } SLO exemption only for force majeure or customer-requested degradation

I’ve attached the redline (MSA_redline_acme_20270630.docx) and a short addendum template. If you’d like, I can push the DocuSign link today so procurement can sign electronically.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_redline_acme_20270630.docx
